answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable bond in a vault before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation. When an agent is caught duplicating identities or laundering trust, the protocol slashes its bond and pays part to those who proved the fraud. A sybil farm must therefore fund every identity separately and risk losing those funds; spreading copies through a canyon of accounts does not multiply influence for free. Even a comet-like burst of new identities faces the same capital cost.
